summary.intent: Fix two related CipherBox macOS bugs: (1) FUSE folder rename requiring elevated permissions and still failing, and (2) web UI folder rename + sync creating duplicate folders instead of renaming in place.
summary.outcome: Both bugs were diagnosed, fixed in `crates/fuse/src/inode.rs` and `write_ops.rs`, covered with unit tests and e2e tests, committed to `fix/fuse-folder-rename`, and PR #466 was created with all 8 automated reviewer comments resolved.

repo: CipherBox uses FUSE-T with an SMB backend on macOS; the SMB layer does its own permission checks against FUSE-reported `getattr` results, so 0o755/0o644 permissions cause rename denials when the SMB client UID doesn't match the FUSE-reported owner — encryption is the real access control layer, not Unix permissions.
Debug sessions are tracked as markdown files in `.planning/debug/` and archived to `.planning/debug/resolved/` when closed; the GSD toolchain reads these via `gsd-tools.cjs`.
The project uses a GSD orchestrator/subagent pattern where debugging is delegated to `gsd-debugger` subagents to preserve main context window budget.
SDK utility scripts live in `packages/sdk-core/scripts/*.mjs` and use direct vault metadata manipulation (load → mutate → republish) mirroring what the web UI does.
E2E desktop tests are split into `test-fuse-operations.sh/.ps1` (local FUSE ops) and `test-cross-client-sync.sh` (SDK-to-FUSE round-trips); both must be kept in sync.
Pre-commit hooks enforce markdownlint and prettier; `pnpm lint:fix` must be run before committing JS/TS files.

code.finding: `populate_folder()` previously matched children by display name only; renames produced duplicate inodes. Fix: build an `ipns_name -> ino` lookup map so stable IPNS identity is checked before falling back to name matching. Also: `log::info!` calls leaked folder/file names to logs — downgraded to `log::debug!` with names removed.
Directory permissions were hardcoded to `0o755`, file permissions to `0o644`. Changed to `0o777`/`0o666` to allow FUSE-T SMB backend to pass write operations regardless of UID mismatch.
Key material was not cleared on error paths. Fixed by wrapping vault key usage in try/finally to ensure cleanup even on exceptions.

Test 7 (FUSE detects rename) had no guard on Test 6 success; added a `rename_ok` flag so Test 7 is skipped entirely on SDK rename failure. Also added `rm -rf` guards to prevent accidental deletion of unintended paths.
Cleanup `rm -rf` calls lacked existence guards; added path validation before removal.

workflow: GitHub CLI auth expiry can be bypassed for a single command with `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh ...` without requiring a full `gh auth login` flow.
Spawning two independent research agents in parallel (FUSE impl + sync logic) before spawning the fix agent avoids serial bottlenecks when root cause spans multiple subsystems.
Running `pnpm lint:fix` after all edits but before staging is necessary — the linter modifies files that were already read, which would cause Edit tool conflicts if done mid-session.

friction: GitHub CLI auth was expired at PR creation time; required `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN` workaround discovered through trial and error.
`pnpm lint:fix` silently modified `rename-folder.mjs` after it had already been read, triggering a harness warning about stale reads.
User had to explicitly prompt for e2e test coverage — the initial fix only added unit tests without proactively covering the desktop e2e layer.
User had to separately request moving resolved debug sessions to the `/resolved` subfolder; the debug workflow didn't automatically archive on status change.
First `/debug` invocation was misrouted to a standard Claude Code debug flow before the GSD orchestrator skill took over, causing a wasted round-trip.
open_items: Bug 1 (FUSE-T SMB permission fix) has no automated test coverage — the 0o777/0o666 change requires manual verification on a live macOS FUSE mount to confirm the Touch ID dialog no longer appears.
Linux and Windows FUSE rename behavior has not been tested; the permission and sync fixes may behave differently on non-macOS platforms.

Two other debug sessions (`fuse-stale-file-after-web-edit`, `google-oauth-tauri-redirect`) were marked resolved and archived but their underlying fixes were not part of this session — resolution status may be aspirational rather than confirmed.
